sentiment.instructions: Judge the overall sentiment the tweet's author conveys: their own attitude or mood, or the clear good/bad nature of the news reported. Label by evaluative tone, not topic; mentions of dates, events or celebrities alone are neutral.

criteria.positive: Author clearly expresses enthusiasm, liking, praise, gratitude, hope, excitement or eager plans (can't wait, love, amazing, going to see X tomorrow!). Also: reported wins, achievements, milestones or historic good news; condolences with prayers/blessings (RIP, may God bless/carry you); sincere well-wishing. Mild but genuine liking counts.
criteria.neutral: Factual reports, schedules, event/meeting/info-session announcements and promo copy with no personal feeling (free, RSVP, come along), spam, questions, fan requests, and hedged opinions (may be, could be). Also light humor, teasing, wry jokes, playful hyperbole (I'm dead, not ready, so afraid of the movie), mild self-deprecation, and mixed or ambivalent feelings. When the tone is joking or observational rather than truly upset, choose neutral.
criteria.negative: Author is genuinely angry, sad, disappointed, disgusted, contemptuous or fearful (sucks, wtf, hate, bummed, :(, boring, shameful), insults or mocks someone harshly, or argues pointedly against a political/religious position. Also news of clearly bad events: attacks, deaths, crimes, arrests, disasters, economic losses, scandals, injuries.
